# Snippets library

This repository holds an end-to-end encrypted Snippets library. The Snippets apps read and write it directly over git; there is no Snippets server.

Every file under `records/` is ciphertext. Names, keywords, tags and bodies can be decrypted only on your own devices. `keys/recovery.json` holds the library key sealed under your offline recovery code; without that code it is useless.

Do not edit, rebase, or force-push this branch by hand. Snippets treats a removed record or a replaced `snippets-sync.json` as a reset of the remote library and stops syncing until you review it on one of your devices.

plainReadme:
# Snippets library (plain text)

This repository holds a Snippets library. The Snippets apps read and write it directly over git; there is no Snippets server.

Ordinary snippets are readable Markdown files directly in `snippets/`: a few lines of front matter (name, keyword, tags, enabled, pinned), then the snippet text. Edit them in any editor or on the web and the apps pick the change up on their next sync. Leave the `id` and `sync` lines alone. A copied file becomes a new snippet, a new Markdown file becomes a new snippet, and deleting a file deletes the snippet on every device. Files in subfolders are ignored, and restoring a deleted snippet's file from history does not bring it back; recreate it in the app.

Everything stays in git history. A snippet that was ordinary once remains readable in old commits even after it is made secure or deleted.

Secure snippets, deletions and snippets carrying sync bookkeeping (such as conflict copies) are encrypted under `records/`; only your own devices can open them. `keys/recovery.json` holds the library key sealed under your offline recovery code.

Do not rebase or force-push this branch. Snippets treats a removed encrypted record or a replaced `snippets-sync.json` as a reset of the remote library and stops syncing until you review it on one of your devices.
